what_i_found.red_arm_PROVEN_for_C5_by_recomputing_fro: The same broken-clone run ALSO had `_finishEquipCommit()`'s `row.slot = slot;` write removed (equip never lands, but the slot-clearing loop just above it still runs). It reported C5 as `ok` under the OLD assertion (`J(wPre.equipped) !== J(wPost.equipped)`) because the array still changed — reed-cutter got unequipped even though the knife never got equipped. THIS IS A REAL DEFECT I FOUND BY RUNNING THE DELETE-THE-FIX ARM: 'the equipped array changed' is not the same claim as 'this row got equipped'. Fixed C5's assertion to check the SPECIFIC item lands (`wPost.equipped.some(e => e.startsWith(itemId + '@'))`). Recomputing that new predicate BY HAND against the already-captured raw numbers from that run — `itemId='hooked-gutting-knife'`, `wPost.equipped=["chitin-cuirass@chest"]`, no `hooked-gutting-knife@` entry — gives `landed=false`, i.e. the REPAIRED C5 assertion would correctly score this broken build FAIL. This is an inline recomputation from evidence already on disk, not a fresh run, and is named as such rather than presented as an executed red-arm run.
what_i_found.d6_repair: Old assertion: back on a one-character query leaves the search view outright (`view !== 'search'`) — round 2's own broken behaviour, encoded as the pass condition. New assertion: one back press removes exactly one character and STAYS in the search view (mode 'journal', view 'search', query length -1), matching the screen's own foot hint ('back to remove one') and the round-3 critic's JX2 sequence. PROVEN BOTH WAYS.
what_i_found.d7_repair: Old check called `goto('journal')` immediately after D6, a no-op when already in 'journal' mode, so it silently re-read D6's own state. New check closes fully to `world` first (asserted `closed.mode === 'world'`), THEN re-opens via `goto('journal')`. Green arm proven; red arm not run (see could_not_do).
what_i_found.h2_repair: `openContainer(name, contents)` does `contents.map(c => ({...c}))`; the old call passed `['bog-iron-maul']`, a string, which spreads into a character map, not an item. Both call sites (H2's transfer test and H3's four bad-header probes) now pass `[{ id: 'bog-iron-maul', count: 1 }]`. Green arm proven; red arm not run.
what_i_found.c5_repair: Two bugs found ONLY by actually running this, not by reading it: (1) the pre-existing weapon regex had no word boundary, so `/bow/i` matched inside 'Mud-slip bowl' (dishware) once `hist-sap-bow` was excluded — fixed with `\b...\b`. (2) the array-changed assertion was too weak, per the red-arm finding above — fixed to check the specific item lands. Split into C5 (skips the known-refused row to test a row that actually equips) and C5b (targets the refused row on its own terms, third outcome via `pushNA`). C5's green+red both proven (red by recomputation); C5b's green proven, red not run.
what_i_found.f1_repair: Split the old compound assertion (place-walk AND view-swap in one `&&`). With `pre.rows.length === 0` (this fixture's actual state), only the view-swap half is asserted, scored `not-applicable`. Proven on the fixed build; no red arm attempted (needs a populated-places fixture, named as follow-up).
what_i_found.t2_repair: T1's touch tap (`touch.swap_right`) leaves the probe on whatever screen is next in the ring after inventory — empirically `map`, confirmed by running the unmodified probe first — with the same 0-places gap as F1. `hasRows` gates the branch: with rows, the original moved/not-moved assertion runs; zero rows scores `not-applicable` UNLESS the mode also changed unexpectedly (still fails then). Proven not-applicable on the fixed build twice, in two separate runs.
what_i_found.third_outcome_mechanism: Added `pushNA(id, ok, detail)`: records `{ pass: ok ? null : false, outcome: ok ? 'not-applicable' : 'fail', detail }`. Exit-code/summary logic changed from `checks.every(c => c.pass)` to explicitly counting `pass === false`, so `null` moves neither the exit code nor the pass tally. The run summary now reports three numbers: passed / not-applicable / failed.
